subject: Comet-7B: elevated 5xx/timeouts — immediate update & mitigation
messages:
From: Tom Lee <tom.lee@orbitanalytics.com>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.company>
Date: Thu, 16 May 2028 08:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: unexpected 503s from Comet-7B during nightly batch

Hi Stephanie —

We started seeing a spike in 503 and timeout errors from Comet-7B during our nightly scoring job starting around 07:45 PDT. The job previously ran without issues; this morning ~15% of requests returned 503 and another ~10% timed out after 8s. We rolled back our side of the pipeline and confirmed the requests hitting Redwood are similar to prior runs (same batch size/context).

Attached is a snippet of the error responses (shortened). Can you confirm if there were any deployments or infra changes on the Redwood side? This is impacting our SLAs for the batch reports.

Thanks,
Tom
Ops Lead, Orbit Analytics
ops@orbitanalytics.com

Hi Tom —

Thanks for the quick heads up and for the snippet — we got it. I’m escalating this to our on-call infra and model-serving team (cc’d).

Initial context from our side: we rolled a small runtime change to the Comet-7B serving kernel at 07:30 PDT earlier today intended to improve long-context KV handling. We have not yet seen this roll trigger errors in Canary, but we’re treating your report as priority.

What we’ll do next:
- Our on-call will collect server-side logs and error traces matching the timestamps you provided.
- If we confirm a regression, we’ll perform an immediate rollback of the kernel change and monitor for recovery.
- I’ll follow up within 60 minutes with an update and an ETA for resolution / mitigation.

Apologies for the disruption — we’ll keep you posted.

-Stephanie Nguyen
Senior Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference
stephanie_nguyen@redwood.company
From: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.company>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.company>, Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.company>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.company>
Date: Thu, 16 May 2028 09:08:44 -0700
Subject: Re: unexpected 503s from Comet-7B during nightly batch (internal)

Internal —

I pulled traces from the serving fleet and matched the timestamps Tom sent. Observations:
- Starting ~07:28 PDT we see a surge of transient 5xx (503/504) correlated with a sharp increase in LRU KV-cache evictions on nodes running the new kernel variant.
- Evictions caused additional cache miss recomputation that overloaded the per-request workers, triggering OOM backpressure on a subset of nodes serving long-context streams.
- Canary did not hit the same long-context distribution so the changes slipped through.

Mitigation applied at 09:02 PDT:
1) Rolled back the kernel patch on the affected shard set (rollout id: rollout-20280516-k1).
2) Temporarily increased per-node worker concurrency limit and disabled aggressive KV prefetch for Comet-7B (config flag: comet7b.kv.prefetch=false).

Post-mitigation: by 09:20 PDT error rate dropped to baseline (~0.3% 5xx) and timeouts returned to normal. I’ve attached a short CSV with the mitigation timeline and error counts.

Next steps I propose:
- Run a targeted replay of long-context jobs against a staging cluster with the kernel change and explicit long-context load.
- Add an automated guard in the rollout pipeline that flags >=1% 5xx in canary for long-context traffic.

I’ll keep monitoring; will post updates here.

- Dev (on-call infra)
From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.company>
To: Tom Lee <tom.lee@orbitanalytics.com>
Cc: dev_patel@redwood.company, sean_gallagher@redwood.company, marcus_lin@redwood.company
Date: Thu, 16 May 2028 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: unexpected 503s from Comet-7B during nightly batch

Tom —

Thank you for the patience — quick update from our engineering team: they identified a correlation between a kernel rollout and increased KV-cache eviction leading to transient overload on a subset of Comet-7B nodes. The team rolled back the change at 09:02 PDT and applied temporary configuration limits. We saw error rates return to baseline by ~09:20 PDT.

What this means for Orbit Analytics:
- Your nightly job (07:45 PDT) overlaps the release window; that exposure likely caused the disruption.
- We have not seen data exposure or request corruption — only request failures/latency.

Attached: mitigation timeline and a short error snippet.
Short-term actions we’ve taken for you:
- Full rollback completed and monitoring on your request keys increased.
- Engineering is scheduling a targeted replay and additional canary tests specifically if you can share a representative sample job (we can run it in our staging environment).

Longer-term plan:
- We will add long-context traffic checks to the canary gating for Comet-7B rollouts.
- Draft postmortem will be shared by EOD today with full RCA and proposed preventive controls.

If you’d like, we can also apply a temporary routing policy to keep your calls on nodes that were not part of the rollback group until we finish the postmortem. Let me know whether you want us to do that.

Again, genuinely sorry for the disruption — we’ll share the postmortem and mitigation artifacts shortly.

-Stephanie
Senior Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference
